title: Contributing
description: How The Upskilling Labs is run, and who it trusts with what: public roles, recognition earned in steps, and who decides. A working draft.

hero.title: How The Labs is run, and who it trusts with what.
hero.lede: Anyone can contribute. Trust is earned in steps, confirmed by peers, and recorded. Each step has a symbol, but the responsibility is the point.
hero.draft: A draft for the board. Only the ambassador program exists today.

ladder.title: Six steps of trust.

rows.how: Improve anything The Labs shares: a playbook, a flyer, the code.
Trained and seated in a role.
rows.trusted: Act in The Labs' name, in that role.

rows.how: Recognized for work The Labs now runs on, with a written citation. The first go to our two steering committees.
A Practitioner in two roles, sponsored by two pin holders.
rows.trusted: Review work in the roles you've practised.

rows.how: Has helped across every core area.
rows.trusted: Approve work, within a written grant from the board.

rows.how: Nominated by Maintainers, confirmed by the board.

ladder.note: Brass for regional work, silver for national. Rank names are drafts. [PLACEHOLDER]

roles.title: Four roles to start.
roles.lede: Each has two stages: Trained, then Practitioner once the role's lead confirms the work.

items.name: Upskiller
items.does: Works on a real local problem with a small team (a pod). A Builder once practised.

items.name: Poderator
items.does: Leads a pod through a Build Cycle.

items.name: Mentor
items.does: Helps pods when they get stuck.

items.name: Ambassador
items.does: Brings people to their first workshop, and gives one talk.

steps.title: It's recorded.
steps.body: Your Lab checks it. HQ records it, with a one-line citation.

steps.title: Pinned.
steps.body: At a regional gathering. The record comes first; the handshake follows.

decides.title: Ranks recognize. Boards decide.
rules: Ranks are permanent. Permissions come with an active seat, which the board grants in writing. Stepping back makes you emeritus.
Ranks carry no vote. The boards run programs, money, people and the brand.
No one can buy a rank, a pin, or a vote. Supporting Members get a button, nothing more.
The one exception to permanence is a serious breach of the Code of Conduct.
